summary: 23-year-old Kansas man hiking with two companions went off-trail into a scree field along the Eldorado Canyon Trail; a shifting boulder estimated at 1,500-3,000 lbs pinned his lower leg. About four hours of technical rescue using airbags, pulleys, and lifts freed him; he suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries and was taken to a hospital
location: Eldorado Canyon Trail, Eldorado Canyon State Park
responding_agency: Rocky Mountain Rescue Group; Rocky Mountain Fire; Boulder Open Space and Mountain Parks; Boulder Fire; Lafayette Fire; North Metro Fire; Boulder County Sheriff's Office
notes: DATE APPROXIMATE: exact incident date not published in either source. SnowBrains says agencies responded "about 1:45 pm last week" (article ~Jan 3, 2019); Unofficial Networks article dated 2018-12-31 treats it as recent news; incident falls in the week of Dec 24-30, 2018. Boulder County Sheriff's Office: victim was hiking with two others, went off trail into open space/scree field; boulder shifted when he put his hand on it. RMRG's Drew Hildner: steep slopes and unsteady boulder field made for a difficult rescue.
